Creatify vs VEXI: AI Video Ads or Your Whole Social Media?
Creatify makes AI video ads with avatars from a product link. VEXI makes and posts your organic social media, and Autopilot runs your week.
Creatify is built to make paid video ads. Here is how it compares with one app that runs your everyday social media.

Creatify is an AI video ad maker. Paste a product link or details and it builds video ads, often with an AI avatar presenting, plus image ads. It can push finished ads to ad accounts. Its pricing page lists Standard at $10 a month with 55 credits, rising to Business at $136 a month, and a no-cost tier of 10 credits a month with watermarked exports. Credits expire after two months.

VEXI (formerly Social Realtr) is an AI content studio that runs social media for entrepreneurs and creators. You describe what you want and it makes the posts, videos, designs and captions, then schedules and publishes them. Plans start at $199 a month, and every plan starts with a 15-day trial.

The difference is the job. Creatify is for advertisers testing paid ads. Your organic feed needs posts, carousels, edited clips of you and your work, captions and a posting rhythm every week. VEXI does that job: you ask, it makes it, and Autopilot posts it. VEXI costs more than Creatify: plans are $199, $399 or $599 a month. What you pay for is the work you no longer do.
Creatify launches paid ads to ad accounts. Its pages say nothing about scheduling organic posts to your own profiles.
VEXI schedules and posts to your connected accounts itself.
Many Creatify videos are presented by AI actors. Some reviewers report faces that change mid-video and voiceovers that do not match.
VEXI edits your own footage and photos into posts, and writes the script and teleprompter if you want to record.
Every video spends credits, and credits expire after two months. Some reviewers report failed generations that still use credits up.
Creatify makes ads when you ask for them. Planning and posting a steady week of content is not what it does.
VEXI Autopilot runs your week ahead: it writes, cuts and posts, and can wait for your approval on everything.
